bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: The standard Scouting and U.S. military regulation bugle is a valveless conical-cylindrical brass aerophone pitched in G with a tuning slide to F.
core_mechanism_bullets: The standard Scouting and U.S. military regulation bugle is a valveless conical-cylindrical brass aerophone pitched in G with a tuning slide to F.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Without valves, all bugle calls use partials 2 through 6 of the harmonic overtone series (written C4, G4, C5, E5, and G5).
core_mechanism_bullets: Without valves, all bugle calls use partials 2 through 6 of the harmonic overtone series (written C4, G4, C5, E5, and G5).
Increasing lip aperture tension and air stream velocity (Bernoulli effect) doubles standing-wave nodes inside the ~4.5-foot tubing.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: Relative to the fundamental pitch (1f), the bugle sounds the 2nd harmonic (octave), 3rd harmonic (perfect fifth), 4th harmonic (double octave), and 5th (major third).

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Crisp military bugle articulation uses 'Tu' or 'Ta' dental tongue releases for single notes and 'Tu-Ku' double-tonguing for rapid sixteenth notes.
core_mechanism_bullets: Crisp military bugle articulation uses 'Tu' or 'Ta' dental tongue releases for single notes and 'Tu-Ku' double-tonguing for rapid sixteenth notes.
Center the mouthpiece rim with roughly 50/50 or 2/3 upper-lip to 1/3 lower-lip placement while maintaining steady abdominal air column support.
